stories.standfirst: For some, a hangover can start an anxious spiral. We spoke to experts about the reasons why.

articles.title: 'That nagging feeling of dread': Is 'hang-xiety' a real thing?
articles.standfirst: For some, a hangover can start an anxious spiral. We spoke to experts about the reasons why.

gist: Hang-xiety is the real anxiety that can accompany a hangover after drinking alcohol.
Brain chemistry shifts, genetics, and shyness can influence how severely people experience hang-xiety.
Experts recommend moderating alcohol intake, drinking water, and reframing thoughts to manage symptoms.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: People wake up after drinking with a throbbing head and a low, gnawing horror or dread about possible social missteps from the night before.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Alcohol affects brain chemicals like GABA and glutamate, sleep patterns, and hormones, triggering rebound anxiety and an exhausting psychological spiral.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Researchers advise moderating drinking, staying hydrated, reframing anxious thoughts as temporary, and seeking medical help if struggling.
